los.text: Perform a structured hand examination and identify signs of injury or disease.
los.html:
• Look, feel, move, function, neurovascular, special tests.
StepDetail
Look (both hands, front and back, pillow)
  • Swelling (MCPs/PIPs: RA; DIPs/PIPs: OA)
  • Deformity (ulnar deviation, swan neck, boutonnière, Z thumb)
  • Heberden's (DIP) and Bouchard's (PIP) nodes
  • Wasting (thenar: median; first dorsal interosseous: ulnar)
  • Scars
  • Nail changes (psoriasis)
  • Skin (tophi, rheumatoid nodules at elbow)
FeelTemperature, tenderness, bimanual squeeze of MCPs (synovitis), joint lines, anatomical snuffbox (scaphoid), sensation
MoveMake a fist, spread fingers, flex/extend wrist (prayer and reverse prayer), thumb movements
FunctionGrip, pinch, picking up a coin, undoing a button, writing
NeurovascularMedian, ulnar, radial motor and sensory tests; radial pulse, capillary refill
Special testsPhalen's and Tinel's (carpal tunnel), Finkelstein's (de Quervain's), Froment's (ulnar)
  • Finish: examine the elbows and the neck; X-ray, bloods (RF, anti-CCP, ESR/CRP).

los.text: Explain the nerve distribution in the hand and its clinical relevance.
los.html:
NerveMotor testSensory area
MedianAbductor pollicis brevis (thumb to ceiling); "OK" sign (anterior interosseous)Palm of lateral 3½ digits (index finger pulp)
UlnarFinger abduction (first dorsal interosseous), Froment's signMedial 1½ digits (little finger pulp)
RadialWrist and finger extensionFirst dorsal web space
  • Relevance: localise lesions (carpal tunnel vs cervical root), assess injuries (wrist lacerations, fractures), protect nerves in procedures.

los.text: Recognise clinical features suggestive of nerve innervation abnormalities
los.html:
FeatureNerve problem
Thenar wasting, weak APB, tingling lateral 3½ fingers worse at night, positive Phalen's/Tinel'sCarpal tunnel syndrome (median)
Hypothenar and interosseous wasting, clawing of ring and little fingers, numb little finger, positive Froment'sUlnar neuropathy (elbow or wrist)
Wrist drop, numb first web spaceRadial nerve palsy (midshaft humerus, "Saturday night palsy")
"Ape hand" (thumb in line with fingers)High median lesion
Glove distribution lossPeripheral neuropathy (diabetes, B12, alcohol)
Dermatomal loss with neck painCervical radiculopathy

los.text: Recognise clinical features suggestive of injury/disease related to the hand
los.html:
FeatureSuggests
Symmetrical MCP/PIP swelling, ulnar deviation, swan neck, boutonnière, nodulesRheumatoid arthritis
Heberden's/Bouchard's nodes, squaring of the thumb baseOsteoarthritis
DIP involvement, nail pitting, dactylitisPsoriatic arthritis
Tophi, acute red hot jointGout
Nodule/cord in palm, fixed flexion of ring/little fingerDupuytren's contracture
Snuffbox tenderness after a fallScaphoid fracture
Mallet fingerExtensor tendon rupture at DIP
Sclerodactyly, calcinosis, Raynaud'sSystemic sclerosis
Swollen, tender, flexed finger (Kanavel signs)Flexor sheath infection: surgical emergency

los.text: Take a focused history from a talkative patient while maintaining control of the consultation
los.html:
TechniqueExample
Signpost the structure upfront"I'd like to hear about your hands, then a few questions about your health"
Summarise to interrupt politely"Can I just stop you there to check I've got this right…"
Focused closed questionsBring the conversation back on track
Acknowledge their concerns"That's clearly important to you; we'll come back to it"
Agenda settingAgree what to cover in the time
RA focusMorning stiffness (>30–60 min), symmetrical small joint swelling, fatigue, function, extra-articular features, family history

los.text: Assess a patient's ability to perform activities of daily living (ADLs) in the context of functional hand or neurological issues.
los.html:
ADLExamples
Personal careWashing, dressing (buttons, zips), grooming, toileting
EatingCutting food, opening jars, holding a cup
Mobility and transfersWalking, stairs, getting up from a chair
Instrumental ADLsCooking, shopping, driving, managing money and medicines, work
Ask aboutAids and adaptations, carers and support, impact on work and hobbies, mood.
WhyGuides treatment goals, referrals (OT, physio, social care) and benefits.

los.text: Demonstrate the ability to perform a neurological examination of the upper limbs with clinical competence, interpret and integrate findings with relevant knowledge to support clinical reasoning, and clearly present these findings to peers or supervisors.
los.html:
• Full routine: see ICM Year 1 › Neurology & cognition › LOs 1 and 2.
Competence =
Smooth sequence: inspection, pronator drift, tone, power, reflexes, coordination, sensation
Interpret: UMN vs LMN pattern, root vs nerve vs neuropathy
Integrate with the history: "These findings suggest a right C6 radiculopathy"
Present clearly: key positives, relevant negatives, summary, differential, next tests (e.g. nerve conduction, MRI cervical spine)
